speaker: alice_brambleby
text: Elbows off my table, Master Kemp, or the story ends where it is.

speaker: will_kemp
text: The story is wider than the table, mistress. By my hose, give me the edge and I will bring the end in with me.

speaker: alice_brambleby
text: You have the edge. You do not have the gravy. Sit in.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Yesterday, after the play. I was Alleyn for a minute. A hamper was the stage, and a stool was the chariot.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: He did get up on it. I was in the room.

speaker: will_kemp
text: And I gave them the line. Holla, ye pampered jades of Asia. The room went as quiet as if I had been the man.

speaker: alice_brambleby
text: Elbows.

speaker: will_kemp
text: I am in. Then I gave the line again, because a chariot is a poor thing if it only rides once.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: And Richard threw a stuffed glove. It hit the hamper by your head.

speaker: will_kemp
text: My head was a near thing. I' faith, he has a good eye and no love of a triumph. That is the end.

speaker: alice_brambleby
text: That is the end I will allow. Your elbows may come back when the plates do.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It was worth the width. He was very like a man on a hamper, which is what he was.

speaker: will_kemp
text: And the Queen's twenty pounds. Has it come?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It is expected.

speaker: alice_brambleby
text: Expected money has eaten several dinners in this house, Master Shakespeare, and never paid for one.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Ha! There is the line of the table, and I will not mend it. I am the loudest man in the room, and I am paying for my own.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: She has the right of it. The twenty pounds is not mine, and it is not yet had. This dinner is fourpence, and the fourpence is mine.

speaker: alice_brambleby
text: Fourpence for you, then. And fourpence for Master Kemp, since he has said so. I will see both before I trust either.

speaker: will_kemp
text: See them. Marry, I like a woman who looks at the coin and not at the story. The story was free. The ling is not.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: There is my fourpence. Leave it where you can see it. I am not eating on a promise.

speaker: alice_brambleby
text: It is on the board. His is beside it. Expected money is not beside them, and it will not be charged, because it never arrives to be charged.

speaker: will_kemp
text: A purse at court, and a glove in a parlour. I know which of them hit anything yesterday.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The glove hit a hamper. The purse has hit nothing of mine. I will say expected once more, and then I have said it.

speaker: alice_brambleby
text: Once is enough. Ling, and small beer, and no scores. When you have eaten, take the afternoon with you.

speaker: will_kemp
text: He is in the play, and he will not tell it. I have told mine. I am the better company until the yard opens.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Tell the hamper as often as you like. Do not tell the twenty pounds as if they were in my purse.

speaker: alice_brambleby
text: They are not in your purse in this house. I have fourpence that says so, and I am content with fourpence.

speaker: will_kemp
text: And I am content, and loud, and paid. Mistress, the end was yours the moment you said elbows. The money is only the proof.
